branches.theme: 1.1 Patterns All Around Us & What is Mathematics?

step_by_step_procedure: Observe regularities in daily events (calendar cycles, financial transactions, architectural tilings, leaf arrangements).
Identify repeating units or structural rules governing the arrangement.
formulas_and_identities: Pattern Rule: Sequence term T_n = f(n)
sub_branches.example_problem: Identify rule in daily calendar days: Sunday, Monday... Repeats every 7 days (Mod 7 cycle).

sub_branches.concept_or_rule: Mathematics as the Search for Patterns
step_by_step_procedure: Combine artistic creativity with scientific rigor to explore structural connections.
Formulate hypotheses about why patterns occur.
Prove generalizations logically to establish universal mathematical laws.
sub_branches.example_problem: Why do consecutive odd sums form square numbers? Proved visually via L-shaped gnomons.

step_by_step_procedure: Counting numbers: Start at 1, add 1 sequentially (1, 2, 3, 4...).
Even numbers: Start at 2, add 2 sequentially (2, 4, 6, 8...).
Odd numbers: Start at 1, add 2 sequentially (1, 3, 5, 7...).
Powers of 2: Start at 1, multiply by 2 successively (1, 2, 4, 8, 16...).
Powers of 3: Start at 1, multiply by 3 successively (1, 3, 9, 27, 81...).
Virahānka (Fibonacci) sequence: Set V_1 = 1, V_2 = 2; add preceding two terms (1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21...).
formulas_and_identities: Virahānka Recurrence: V_n = V_{n-1} + V_{n-2} (V_1 = 1, V_2 = 2)

branches.theme: 1.3 Visualising Number Sequences through Geometric Arrays

step_by_step_procedure: Triangular numbers: Arrange dots in equilateral triangles (1, 3, 6, 10, 15...).
Square numbers: Arrange dots in square grids (1, 4, 9, 16, 25...).
Hexagonal numbers: Arrange dots in concentric regular hexagonal rings (1, 7, 19, 37...).
Stack 2D square dot layers into 3D cubic prisms.
An n x n x n cube array contains n^3 dots.

sub_branches.concept_or_rule: L-Shaped Gnomon Decompositions & Sum of Odd Numbers
step_by_step_procedure: Start with a single dot (1x1 square).
Enlarge to a 2x2 square by adding an L-shaped gnomon layer of 3 dots.
Enlarge to a 3x3 square by adding a gnomon of 5 dots.
Conclude that summing the first n odd numbers equals n^2.
Identify the central peak integer n in series 1 + 2 + ... + n + ... + 2 + 1.
Note that combining two triangles T_{n-1} and T_n with peak n forms n^2.
Take two adjacent triangular dot arrays T_{n-1} and T_n.
Align them along their diagonal boundary.
Observe that they form a complete n x n square dot grid.
Connect n points where every pair is joined by a segment (Complete Graph).
Count total connections: equals the (n-1)-th triangular number T_{n-1}.
sub_branches.example_problem: 6 people meet and everyone shakes hands once: T_5 = 5(6)/2 = 15 handshakes.

step_by_step_procedure: Start with an equilateral triangle (Iteration 0).
Replace middle third of each side with an outward equilateral triangular point.
Repeat process infinitely to generate expanding perimeter with finite area.
formulas_and_identities: Number of sides at iteration k: N_k = 3 x 4^k
sub_branches.example_problem: Find side count at 2nd iteration: 3 x 4^2 = 48 sides.
